out.other_title: Open: oracle models, regret notions and equilibria suited to language games
out.rationale: Chen et al. propose games with very large action spaces as a model for language games and AI debate, and ask for notions of equilibrium better suited to these games. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that, for a probabilistic decision problem that has a valid proof system, a profile is a valid interactive proof system iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of a nip game, while noting worst-case losses and Stackelberg equilibria are hard to learn. The cited passages do not show that nip games are language games or AI debate games with very large action spaces, so Theorem 8 is not shown to answer Chen et al.'s call, and Chen et al.'s call does not bear on Theorem 8; neither bears on the other's claim.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: notions of equilibrium for games used as formal models of AI debate or interactive proofs; the cited passages do not show that nip games are games with very large action spaces of the kind Chen et al. study

out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols in verifier-leading sequential PVG formulations where the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that for a probabilistic decision problem with a valid proof system a profile is a valid interactive proof iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of a nip game, and note the challenge of learning to minimise worst-case rather than expected loss. The cited passages show two parallel results, not one building on the other.

text: Theorem 8 states that for a probabilistic decision problem that has a valid proof system, a strategy profile is a valid interactive proof system if and only if it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of the nip game. The authors note this leaves two difficulties: learning to minimise the worst-case rather than expected loss, and finding a Stackelberg equilibrium.
title: Theorem 8: for problems with a valid proof system, valid interactive proofs = approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of nip
